title: Measure the answer, not the vibe
summary: Score a fixed evaluation set, separate regressions from noise, and analyze failures by category.

scenario.briefing: The advising assistant ships prompt changes weekly. Reviews rely on a few impressive examples, and a regression reached students because nobody compared the new prompt with a fixed set. Build the scorer and choose an evaluation set that can catch the next regression.

objectives.description: Score a fixed set with exact, reproducible comparisons.
Choose an evaluation set with coverage and regressions.
Explain error analysis and threshold decisions.

hints: An evaluation needs fixed inputs and expected outputs.
Compare structured values canonically, not by display text.
Report which cases failed, not only the pass rate.
Keep representative, adversarial, and regression cases; never tune on the same set you report.

misconceptions.feedback: A set of easy examples cannot reveal regressions. Add adversarial, boundary, and previously failing cases.

misconceptions.description: Treating one impressive answer as proof of quality.
misconceptions.feedback: One answer is an anecdote. Quality claims need a fixed set, a threshold, and repeated runs.

misconceptions.description: Tuning the prompt on the same cases used for the reported score.
misconceptions.feedback: Tuning on the reported set overfits it. Hold out cases or refresh the set after changes.

sections.title: An evaluation is a test suite
sections.body: Fix the inputs, expected outputs, and comparison rule. Run the same set for every prompt or model change so differences measure the change rather than the sample.

sections.title: Coverage beats volume
sections.body: A useful set includes ordinary cases, boundaries, adversarial inputs, and cases that failed before. Random volume without coverage hides the failures that matter.

sections.title: Analyze errors by category
sections.body: A pass rate alone does not say what to fix. Group failures by retrieval, instruction following, formatting, or refusal, then inspect examples in each group. Keep a held-out set for the final claim.

steps.title: Score the evaluation set
steps.prompt: Edit evaluate.js. scoreCases(cases) returns { total, passed, failed } where a case passes when its actual value equals its expected value structurally, regardless of object key order. failed keeps the input order of ids.
hints: Compare structured values with a canonical serialization.
Sort object keys before comparing so key order does not matter.
Push each failing id in input order and return the counts.

tests.description: Compares nested objects regardless of key order.
tests.name: scoreCases

steps.title: Choose the evaluation set
steps.prompt: Which set gives the most useful signal for a prompt change?
hints: A set should cover more than easy examples.
Previously failing cases protect against regressions.
Held-out cases keep the final score honest.
Choose representative, adversarial, boundary, and regression cases.

quiz.prompt: Select the evaluation set you would keep.

options.label: Representative cases, boundaries, adversarial inputs, and prior failures, with a held-out subset
The one demo that impressed the team
The five most recent user questions
Only cases generated by the same model

quiz.explanation: Coverage plus held-out cases measures both regressions and generalization. A demo or the latest questions overfit the moment.

steps.title: Report and improve
hints: A pass rate is a summary, not a diagnosis.
Group failures before choosing a fix.
Tuning and reporting should not use the same cases.
Select error categories, thresholds, held-out sets, and reruns; reject tuning on the reported set.

statements.label: Grouping failures by cause points to the next engineering change.
A change should meet a pass threshold before it ships.
Held-out cases keep the reported score from being optimistically biased.
The same set should be rerun for every prompt or model change.
Tuning on the reported set is fine because it improves the score.

steps.explanation: Evaluation supports decisions when the set is stable, covered, held out from tuning, and analyzed by failure category.

accessibility.summary: Every control is reachable by keyboard, and the checks report text results rather than color alone.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between controls. Space selects a choice, and Ctrl+Enter runs or submits the active check.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each option, finding, and test announces its label, state, and whether the check passed.
